title: Wireless Network Security
objective: Study-guide review — CISSP — Domain 4: Communication and Network Security: Wireless Network Security.

items: WEP — Wired Equivalent Privacy; broken, never use (RC4, static keys)
WPA — Wi-Fi Protected Access; improved but still uses RC4 (TKIP)
WPA2 — Uses AES-CCMP; current minimum standard
WPA3 — Uses SAE (Simultaneous Authentication of Equals); strongest

blocks.text: From Shon Harris: "Wireless encryption at the Data Link Layer" operates at Layer 2. ⚠️ Exam Trap: WEP is COMPLETELY broken and should never be used. WPA2 with AES is the MINIMUM acceptable standard. WPA3 is preferred for new deployments.

items: Evil Twin — Rogue AP mimicking legitimate network
Deauthentication — Forcing clients to disconnect (DoS or capture handshake)
War Driving — Scanning for wireless networks while driving
WPS Attack — Exploiting Wi-Fi Protected Setup PIN (brute-forceable)

rows: Fake AP with same SSID; captures credentials
Sends deauth frames to disconnect users
